doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Responsibility in show pit bands and live versus recorded music
summary: He describes the drummer's responsibility in pit work, subbing in A Chorus Line, and the lost energy of pre-recorded tracks.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That’s a big responsibility in a pit band, isn’t it?

Very large. Everybody can be making clams, but if the drummer doesn’t make it, it train wrecks. I feel a big responsibility when I take a show. Recently I did a show where I ran into a situation after being in this business many years, where I subbed for a drummer and I could read the part fine, but he had the drumset screwed down to the stage in the manner that he played it. And it was next to impossible for me to play. It was a big responsibility and people were asking me, are you okay? But it was just impossible to negotiate.

I subbed in “A Chorus Line” in New York City, and the drummer is in literally a plexiglass box, totally, with a little T.V. monitor. And it’s totally different from a jazz situation, where you can feel and respond from somebody, it’s just like—
What are you seeing on the monitor in that situation?
Because I had to catch certain things. I could see the conductor.

Things have changed some. Some of the shows to come to this area, first of all of course the pit bands are shrinking in size, it’s just too bad, but on occasion they’ve even had some of the stuff pre-recorded, so that the whole thing is turned around, where the conductor is conducting to a pre-recorded track, and the singers are singing it.

The difference with that and if I may, is the lack of energy. If you see a show with a live band there, there’s an energy that’s communicated, not only to the audience but to the dancers, the actors. And it just comes out. If there’s a pre-recorded tape, I think there’s a lack of energy, and the overall performance is not that of having live musicians there. Somewhat like having a D.J. at a wedding.
